failed_calls_retries.assessment: There were 88 total tool calls and 2 failed calls, for a 2.27% failure rate. The longest failure run was 1 because each failed reroute was followed by an APPLIED call. Both failures were the same validation class—reroute corners that could not connect orthogonally to the edge endpoints—so the error class recurred after it had already been explained at turn 27. Both instances were subsequently corrected. No resolve_request or finalize call was rejected, and session metadata records no harness retry.

There were two render→adjust→render loops: turn 11 to turn 77 and turn 77 to turn 86. The second loop is meaningful QA: the turn-77 render was followed by label, containment, fitting, and description adjustments, then a clean turn-86 render. However, most dense grading and routing work from turns 31–76 proceeded without a region-specific close-up, so the perception practice was adequate but not exemplary.

economy.assessment: The session committed 49 patch operations through 88 tool calls in about 10.14 minutes, remaining within both the 15-minute and 300-turn budgets. The work was substantial but proportionate to a detailed orchestration diagram. There were localized label and route refinements, but no object-level build-delete-rebuild cycle, repeated NO-OP, abandon, or turn-budget exhaustion. The fan-out label was temporarily cleared and later restored during QA, but this was a lint-driven label strategy change rather than destructive board reconstruction.
